— Basic driving and observation","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Basic driving and observation

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
No manual alone teaches driving skill; safe operation comes only through instruction, practice and applied choices. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
Distraction means eyes off the road, hands off the wheel or mind off driving, while ninety percent of decisions rest on vision. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
Crash risk rises with any side task or glance away, spanning texting, phones, food, passengers, grooming, reading, navigation, video, audio controls and fatigue. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A01
Texting is the worst distraction because it combines manual, visual and cognitive load at once. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A01
A text costs five seconds of eyes-off-road, which the handbook likens to crossing a football field blindfolded at fifty-five miles per hour. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A01
So-called multitasking is rapid single-task switching, and every distraction raises crash risk for all road users. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A01
Never text or call while driving, speak up as a passenger, and urge phone-free driving on others. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A01
Most Montana cities ban texting and phoning while driving; handle needs only after pulling over and stopping. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A01
Keep eyes on the road, hands on the wheel, everyone buckled, and alcohol out of driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A02
Start per the owner manual with the brake set, manuals out of gear with clutch as needed, and automatics in park. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A02
Accelerate gently since hard starts spin wheels and slide the car, and shift manuals without over-revving or stalling. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A02
Grip opposite sides of the wheel, such as nine-and-three or eight-and-four with wheel-mounted airbags, for comfort and control. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A02
Look far down the road to anticipate steering needs in time for smooth, safe moves. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A02
Corner with hand-over-hand grip and straighten by hand, never palming one-handed or letting the wheel slip. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A03
Watch the speedometer since drivers misjudge speed, especially leaving fast roads for slow local streets. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A03
Follow posted limits for safety and drive below them on bad roads or weather; standard limits sit in the driving-rules chapter. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A03
Anticipate stops early because sudden braking risks skids, lost control and rear-end hits from behind. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A03
Ease off or change lanes early to avoid stopping at all, or at least to stop gradually and safely. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A03
Most driving depends on vision, and missed sights top crash causes, so scan ahead, sides and behind with headlights in poor light. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A03
Never look away more than a few seconds; pull over to read maps or handle anything demanding eyes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A03
Avoid phone and radio use in motion even hands-free, and never drive wearing headphones or earbuds that block horns and sirens. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A03
Pass roadside incidents without staring or slowing to gawk, keeping eyes ahead and clearing the scene promptly and safely. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A04
Scan ahead, to the sides and behind to spot problems, road users, warning signs and direction signs early. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A04
Look at least ten seconds ahead to brake and steer early, saving fuel, smoothing traffic and holding a straighter line. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A04
Ten seconds spans about one city block in town and about four blocks or a quarter mile on highways. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A04
Search the sides constantly since crossings can appear anywhere, especially at intersections and railroad tracks. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A05
Intersections include any merging or crossing point; look left, right and across before entering or starting. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A05
Left across oncoming traffic needs a safe gap, a clear destination street, and one last oncoming check; one-way to one-way lefts are allowed unless barred. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A05
Right turns need clear left and no conflicting oncoming lefts, plus a pedestrian check; right on red is allowed unless barred. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A05
Never trust signals to stop cross traffic; watch for red-light runners, especially just after green. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A05
If stopped at an intersection with a blocked cross-street view, edge forward slowly until crossing traffic can be seen, allowing crossing drivers to see the vehicle front and warn if needed. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A05
Scan sides near shops, lots, work zones, sidewalks, playgrounds and school yards where entries are likely. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A05
Look up and down every rail crossing without assuming no train; at multi-track crossings wait until the passed train clears in case another hides behind it. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F34 | anchor: A05
Check behind often, especially in heavy traffic and before lane changes, slowdowns, backing or long downhill runs. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F35 | anchor: A06
Lane changes, merges and curb entries all require confirming the target lane is empty beside and behind. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F36 | anchor: A06
Signal the lane change, clear mirrors for occupants and passers, then check the blind spot over the shoulder. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F37 | anchor: A06
Glance quickly without leaving the road ahead, rechecking mirrors and the blind spot just before moving. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F38 | anchor: A06
Check the far lane for converging drivers and watch for hard-to-see bikes, motorcycles and pedestrians, especially entering from curbs or driveways. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F39 | anchor: A06
Check behind on every slowdown, particularly sudden ones or where followers least expect braking. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F40 | anchor: A06
Leave the curb with a signal, a left-shoulder look, and a safe gap. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F41 | anchor: A07
Night vision falls while ninety percent of decisions still need sight, so slow down for road, car and weather conditions. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-F42 | anchor: A07
Burn headlights from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, or whenever people and vehicles vanish inside five hundred feet. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-F43 | anchor: A07
Upper beams must reveal people and vehicles three hundred fifty feet out and lower beams one hundred feet; dim within one thousand feet of oncoming traffic and five hundred behind followed vehicles. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-F44 | anchor: A07
Meet night traffic by watching the right road edge instead of the beams, and check the dimmer when flashed. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0065]

Misconceptions: Hands-free is still distracted; mirrors never clear the blind spot alone.
Mnemonics: Authored cue: eyes up, scan wide, signal, shoulder-check, ease down.
Glossary: Blind spot; following interval; high beam; low beam; rubbernecking; hand-over-hand.
Dynamic facts: Posted limits and local device bans vary; obey the displayed control and local ordinance.
